macro.text: October PPI +0.3% vs +0.4% expected, core +0.3% in line; 6.5% a year, the highest since Nov 2022. December hike fully priced (25 bp ~87%, 50 bp ~13%).
10-year yield ~5.14% (+4 bp) after PPI; feed 5.16%, 30-year 5.49%. FT: Treasuries set for their worst week since April 2025's 'liberation day'.
Chicago Fed's Goolsbee: the Fed 'has definitely got work to do' on inflation; AI data center build 'starting to spread out of its lane'.
Bessent: 'a lot of leakage' of Nvidia chips to China; five agencies backed putting Singapore's Megaspeed on the entity list, Commerce has not. NVDA −3.5%.
IEA: oil supply now exceeds demand for the first time since the Iran war as Gulf shipments rebound; inventories +52M barrels in October. Brent still 96.83 (+1.0%), WTI 89.36.

bigNames.text: Outlook and Teams outage runs into a second day; Microsoft says email queues are 'approaching normal levels'.

briefs.read: Risk-off in tech, 43 minutes into the session: QQQ −1.9% (675.28), SPY −0.9% (750.05), IWM −1.0% (275.73) at 10:13; VIX 19.26 (+0.56). Opening gains faded fast as Nvidia (−3.5%) slid under its premarket low and chips broke (SMH −4.3%). PPI is out: 0.3% vs 0.4% expected, core 0.3% in line, but 6.5% a year, the most since 2022; 10-year 5.16%. No more red events. Wait for SMH and QQQ to hold a 15-minute low before trusting any chip bounce.

briefs.scenario: Scenario in play: if the Fed signals a December hike (100% priced, Goolsbee says 'work to do', PPI 6.5% a year), the report expects banks and cash to lead and CRWV, NBIS, ORCL and high-multiple software to lag.

earnings.result: Adj. EPS $1.40 vs $1.33 expected, revenue $18.5B vs $18.1B (+24%); Q2 guide $18.0–18.2B vs $17.88B; FY revenue raised to $74.8–75.8B. But adj. gross margin 65.6% (−250 bp, memory costs) and product orders +21% vs +35% last quarter.
earnings.meaning: A beat sold on margins and slower orders: AI networking demand is there, but memory costs bite the buyers, as the report's memory-squeeze row says.

earnings.result: Adj. EPS $4.16 vs $4.05 expected, revenue $10.41B vs $10.30B (+53%); Q1 guide about $11.1B vs $10.89B. At least 10 firms cut targets on sector multiples, all kept buy ratings.
earnings.meaning: Orders are fine; the stock trades the chip group's multiple, not its own numbers.

briefs.flowNote: Money is leaving chips and high-growth tech hard (SMH −4.3%, XLK −2.9%, ARKK −2.8%, IGV −1.4% since yesterday's close at 10:13): the Nvidia-alternative trade that ran AMD +45% and AVGO +25% in five days is unwinding, Bessent's chip-leakage comments keep China export risk live, Cisco's margin squeeze and Broadcom's downgrade hit the suppliers, and a 10-year above 5.1% after PPI weighs on long-duration names. It is going to communication (XLC +0.8%), staples (XLP +0.7%) and financials (XLF +0.3%) as the hike is priced in; energy is barely up (XLE +0.2%) with Brent higher but the IEA calling a surplus.

bigPicture: The rotation from Nvidia into AMD and Broadcom (+45% and +25% in five days) is being unwound in one morning; with no new AMD news, this is positioning, not fundamentals.

Rates keep tightening the screws: PPI's 6.5% annual rate, Goolsbee's 'work to do' and a 10-year above 5.1% leave a December hike fully priced and Treasuries on course for their worst week since April 2025.
Good prints are not enough: Cisco, Applied Materials and Nebius all beat this week and were sold; the market punishes margin pressure (memory costs) and spending that outruns revenue.
Money hides in communication, staples and financials; energy is only slightly up because the IEA now sees an oil surplus.
snapshot.takeaway: This edition went out 43 minutes after the open, so the gaps have already traded. Chips are in a forced unwind with no new company news behind most of it; the cleanest tell is whether SMH and NVDA can reclaim their premarket lows (NVDA 162.71). Until they do, rallies in chips are retests, and Friday afternoon fades have been the pattern this week.

sectors.text: SMH −4.3%: AMD −9.5% and AVGO −6.0% (Redburn downgrade) give back the Nvidia-alternative run; NVDA −3.5% under its premarket low on Bessent's chip-leakage remarks; SNDK −8.4% on a Kioxia NAND pricing warning; MU −4.9%, TSM −2.9%.
CRWV −9.9% on target cuts (Stifel $60, DA Davidson $45) and Microsoft's neocloud review; ORCL −4.2%. A fully priced hike and a 5.16% 10-year are the report's worst case for leveraged builders.

Cisco beat and raised but fell 5.2% on a 250 bp gross-margin drop and slower orders; Applied Materials −6.2% on sector multiple cuts despite an above-consensus guide. Cerebras (+10%) is the exception.
IGV −1.4%: Microsoft −0.8% as its Outlook and Teams outage enters a second day; rising yields weigh on multiples. Palo Alto +3.5% on a KeyBanc upgrade is a bright spot.
Brent 96.83 (+1.0%), WTI 89.36 (+0.7%), XLE +0.2% after +4.4% in five days. The IEA says supply now exceeds demand as Gulf shipments rebound, a headwind for the E&Ps if it sticks.

bigNames.text: Longest weekly losing streak since 2012, ~$1.7T of value gone; third affair allegation reported; Lutnick under scrutiny. Earnings Nov 17.
FAA nationwide ground stop at about 4:10 PM over air-traffic communication issues; airlines react Monday.
Microsoft 'deeply sorry' for the ~24-hour Outlook and Teams outage; easing, recovery timeline uncertain. Cerebras announced a Microsoft cloud deal.

briefs.read: Chip unwind held: SPY's 9:30 print (760.12) was the high, the low came at 11:35 (745.20), then a grind back to 754.25 (−0.38%); QQQ −1.20%. AMD, AVGO, CSCO took the puts side all day; NVDA fell to 158.39, then closed on 162.71 (162.85); CRWV and CBRS broke down, then reversed up. Money left SMH (−3.0%) for XLP, XLC, XLE. FAA ground stop after close. No red events Monday; NVDA reports Tue.
